featured_reviews.name: padma rajasekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
had a very disappointing experience with Dr. Zubair regarding my foot pain.
During my first visit, he advised me to take an X-ray, which I did at his hospital after paying consultation and X-ray charges. The X-ray was normal. To further identify the issue, he then suggested an MRI and specifically gave me a slip and contact number of a particular MRI centre (Pulse), asking me to inform him once the report was ready.
When I contacted that centre, the cost quoted was ₹5000. I checked with Aarthi Scan Centre for the same MRI, where the cost was ₹3800, so I chose Aarthi Scan and completed my MRI there. I sent the report to the number provided by the doctor, but there was no response. Assuming the doctor might be busy, I went directly to the hospital.
At the reception, I was questioned about why I had taken the MRI at a different centre instead of the one suggested. I clearly asked whether the doctor would refuse to see an outside report and mentioned that if so, I would leave. I did not get a clear answer.
When I met the doctor, instead of discussing my foot problem, he focused mainly on why I took the MRI at Aarthi Scan. After briefly looking at the report, he said it was “not clear” and that he could not give treatment, and then suggested another doctor. He also said that if that doctor advised a repeat MRI, it must be done only at Pulse centre.
In my second visit (within 5 days), no examination or treatment was given. The entire discussion was about why MRI should be done at the suggested centre and not elsewhere. For this visit also, I was charged consultation fees.
My concern is simple: if outside MRI reports are not acceptable, this should be clearly informed to patients during the first visit itself. This would save patients’ time, money, and mental stress. I paid consultation fees twice and X-ray charges, yet received no treatment or proper discussion about my actual foot condition.
With the same MRI report, I consulted another doctor (not the one suggested here), and treatment was started immediately. I am now recovering.
I am sharing this review purely based on my experience, not commenting on the doctor’s medical knowledge, but on the way my case was handled.

10 Common Conditions Treated by an Orthopedic Surgeon

Bone and joint problems can affect your daily activities, movement, and overall quality of life. Consulting an orthopedic specialist at the right time can help you recover faster and prevent complications. If you are searching for an experienced Orthopedic Surgeon in Kandivali, Dr. Abhishek Chaturvedi provides expert orthopedic care tailored to individual needs.

Here are 10 common conditions treated by an orthopedic surgeon:

Knee Pain – Persistent pain, stiffness, or reduced mobility.
Arthritis – Joint inflammation causing pain and discomfort.
Fractures – Proper treatment for broken or cracked bones.
Sports Injuries – Ligament, muscle, and tendon-related injuries.
Shoulder Pain – Including frozen shoulder and tendon problems.
Back Pain – Chronic or injury-related spinal discomfort.
Frozen Shoulder – Restricted movement and stiffness.
Joint Stiffness – Reduced flexibility affecting daily life.
Ligament & Tendon Injuries – Common after falls or sports activities.
Hip Pain – Pain affecting walking and mobility.

If you are experiencing orthopedic symptoms, consult Dr. Abhishek Chaturvedi, Orthopedic Surgeon in Kandivali, for expert evaluation & personalized treatment.

Many people confuse hip pain with lower back pain because both can cause discomfort around the lower body, difficulty walking, and stiffness. However, understanding the difference is important because the treatment approach for each condition can be very different.

Signs of Hip Pain

Hip pain is usually felt:
✔ In the groin area
✔ Around the hip joint
✔ On the side of the thigh
✔ While walking, climbing stairs, or getting up from a chair

Patients with hip joint problems may also notice reduced mobility and stiffness in the hip.

Signs of Lower Back Pain

Lower back pain is more commonly felt:
✔ Around the spine or lower back
✔ While bending or lifting
✔ Radiating toward the legs in some cases
✔ Along with numbness or tingling sensations

Back-related pain often becomes worse with prolonged sitting or certain movements.

When Should You Consult a Specialist?

You should seek medical evaluation if you experience:
⚠️ Persistent pain while walking
⚠️ Difficulty climbing stairs
⚠️ Stiffness in hip movement
⚠️ Pain affecting sleep or daily life
